venue.name: Beacon Hill Children's Farm
venue.description: The Beacon Hill Children's Farm is a small family-run farm inside Beacon Hill Park in Victoria, BC, that has been operated since 1985 by the Koenders family in conjunction with the Beacon Hill Farm Society. It is home to more than a hundred farm animals including goats, pigs, Jacob sheep, miniature donkeys, guinea pigs, alpacas, ducks, chickens and birds, and includes a goat petting area visitors may enter.
venue.seasonal_notes: The farm runs a public season and an off season; the Plan Your Visit page still reads "The farm is open now for the season 2024!", so the page appears not to have been updated for the current year.

programs.name: Group visit
programs.description: School, childcare and summer camp groups, or any group of 10 or more participants and those requiring supervision, are asked to book ahead by email or phone because the farm and the goat petting area have a maximum visitor capacity; booked groups get priority during busy times. The booking inquiry must include the group leader's name and group name, a phone number, the number of children and accompanying supervisors, and the requested day and time, and the booking is only valid once confirmed by email or phone. Admission is by donation with suggested amounts of $6.00 for adults and $5.00 for children; no separate group rate is published. There is no bathroom inside the farm and the nearest public washroom is about a 3 minute walk, so groups are asked to allow time for it. Group leaders are responsible for their group's behaviour and are asked to brief participants on the farm rules (walking only, quiet voices, no feeding the animals, constant adult supervision).
programs.evidence: For school, childcare, or summer camp groups – or any group with 10 or more participants and those requiring supervision
